title: Ealag and Torcall Tochlair are promised by their households
summary: Two households of the hill above Dùn ìseal, who share a slope and a spring, treat a match between Ealag and Torcall Tochlair as already settled. Torcall's mother carries the salt across to ask for it in the old way.

title: The salt is refused
summary: Torcall's mother brings the salt back unaccepted. The elders of Ealag's household give her no reason, only that the match cannot be, and she comes home with her face set as it had never been set before.

title: Torcall is turned away at every door
summary: Torcall Tochlair goes himself to Ealag's father and her uncles and is told, in the same three words each time, that the marriage cannot be. None of them will say why, and he cannot tell whether none of them know it or all of them have sworn silence.

title: Ealag's mother weeps and will not say
summary: Ealag asks her own mother for the reason and is told only to stop asking, and her mother weeps, which Ealag has never seen her do, not even at a burying.

title: Ealag given to a household of Muileann òg
summary: Ealag is married to Donnchadh, a fisher of the ford town of Muileann òg, who asks for her honestly and does not learn of the earlier match for three years.

title: Torcall hears of the black hill in the east
summary: Torcall Tochlair, restless in the gallery under the mountain, hears from traders of ground in the east with a look of coal about it, and begins asking the older diggers whether the vein is the island's only one.

title: The lines first recited at Muileann òg
summary: Before any match is spoken at the fair, a household stands and gives its line aloud, seven names back on either side, so a forbidden blood may be named before the salt is carried. Ealag hears it and thinks of the four shut mouths that refused her.

title: Ealag tells Donnchadh of Torcall
summary: That evening Ealag tells her husband of the match that was refused her. He says only that it explains a look she sometimes wears at fair-time, and asks nothing further.

title: Lachann agrees to go east with his brother
summary: Torcall's younger brother Lachann, easier in temper but loyal to him, agrees to go east to the black hill with two other restless diggers, meaning to see Torcall satisfied and brought home again.

title: Lachann buried at the trench's mouth
summary: Torcall will not have his brother carried elsewhere and buries him where he fell, at the mouth of the trench on the black hill. The other man killed with him is carried home by his own people.

title: Torcall builds a shelter at the trench
summary: When the other diggers pack their tools and go back to the gallery under the mountain, Torcall Tochlair stays, and builds himself a turf shelter at the trench's edge for the winter.

title: Word of Torcall reaches Ealag
summary: A trader who stopped at the black hill brings word to Muileann òg of a man sitting alone beside an open trench with his brother in the ground nearby, still saying he means to find the coal.

title: The saying of the vein's choosing begins to travel
summary: After the second opening strikes only unbroken common stone, it is said across the island that the vein under the mountain is alone of its kind and chose its one place the way the seven coals are said to have chosen theirs.

title: The will for a third opening goes out of the island
summary: No elder forbids a third trench outright, but the wish for one fades everywhere at once, the way the wish for a refused match fades in two households without a word spoken between them.

title: Ealag dies at Muileann òg
summary: Ealag dies in her own bed at Muileann òg with her children about her, having lived her whole life after the refusal without the reason for it.

title: A household gathers at the black hill's foot
summary: Folk who come to the black hill for one reason or another begin to stay, since the ground is as good as any and the man who keeps the open trench asks nothing of them.

title: Torcall Tochlair dies at the trench
summary: Torcall Tochlair dies at the black hill and is buried beside his brother at the trench's mouth. The household he gathered keeps the ground and does not fill the trench in.
